messages:
elena: Hey everyone — following up from today’s all-hands. Opening a live Q&A thread for any questions on our mission, positioning, competitors, and roadmap follow-ups. I’ll chime in over the next 30m. :wave:

matt_p: Thanks Elena. Quick and high-level: are we still 'developer-first' as the core GTM? or do we plan to tilt more enterprise-heavy in the next 12 months? :thinking:

elena: Short answer: developer-first remains our north star. Long answer: we’ll invest enterprise motion where customers show clear demand (security, SLAs, private deployments). The product will stay consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so engineering teams get the same API regardless of tier.

sophia_r: How do we articulate that externally without scaring off enterprise buyers who expect a different sales pitch?

elena: We lead with developer experience + predictable economics. For enterprise conversations, we overlay compliance, support, and contractual SLAs. Messaging: "developer-friendly, enterprise-ready."

raj: On competition — what’s the simple differentiator vs big cloud-managed endpoints and emerging inference runtimes?

elena: Three practical pillars: 1) predictable unit economics (cost controls + Optimize tooling), 2) unified runtime across environments (no surprise changes between hosted vs private), 3) ops-first reliability (fallbacks, rollout primitives). That combination is hard to replicate quickly.

calvin: Do we have a short bullet list we can use in customer calls vs top 3 competitors? (engineering teams keep asking)

elena: Yes — shareable bullets: "1) Same API across hosted/dedicated/private; 2) Cost controls: batching, caching, quantization profiles surfaced in console; 3) SLO-backed Dedicated with predictable throughput; 4) First-class evals and rollback to prevent quality regressions." I’ll drop a slide after this thread.

priya: For the roadmap ask — are we prioritizing new model types (multimodal) or deeper infra features (autoscaling, KV cache improvements) next quarter?

elena: Prioritization is workload-driven. Near-term infra: autoscaling and cache diagnostics (to drive immediate cost/latency wins). Medium-term: experiments for multimodal endpoints, but only if we can ship with the same reliability story.

matt_p: Follow-up: pricing — any plans to move away from per-token for hosted, or add plan-level discounts for Dedicated? Sales is asking for clearer answers.

elena: We’re keeping per-token for Hosted but will add more flexible committed-capacity plans for Dedicated (monthly/annual) and negotiated enterprise terms. We also plan credits/discounts based on sustained throughput and cache hit rates.

calvin: On partner ecosystem — how aggressive are we on bringing ISVs to build on top of Redwood vs keeping it mostly direct?

elena: Strategic partners where they add distribution or deep industry integrations. We’ll prioritize partner work that reduces friction for regulated verticals (finserv, healthcare) and channel partners for regions we don’t operate in.

raj: One last product-level: how do we decide when to onboard a new open model into our catalog? Is it purely perf/cost metrics or also licensing/community traction?

elena: Combination: must meet performance/profile thresholds on our infra, show consistent quality on representative prompts, and have clear licensing for commercial use. We also weigh community adoption and maintainer activity.

priya: Small ask — can leadership publish a short FAQ summarizing these points for customer-facing teams?

elena: Yes — I’ll work with Matt to publish a 1-page FAQ + 4 bullets for sales play and drop it into the sales enablement folder by EOD tomorrow.

matt_p: Thanks! I’ll turn the FAQ into a single slide set for calls.

deploy-bot: Notice: all-hands recording uploaded to drive (link: https://drive.internal/redwood/all-hands/176850).

elena: Great thread — appreciate the concise questions. If you have follow-ups that need more than a chat answer, ping me or book 15m. Otherwise I’ll post the FAQ and the slide bullets shortly. :rocket:
